name: PROPER
description: PROPER capitalizes the first letter of each word in a text string and converts all other letters to lowercase.
tldr: Title-cases each word in a string.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text or cell reference to convert to title case.

basicExample.explanation: The first letter of each word is uppercased and the rest lowercased.

advancedExamples.title: Clean up imported names
advancedExamples.explanation: Each word's first letter is capitalized for a clean display.

advancedExamples.title: Mixed case product codes
advancedExamples.explanation: PROPER capitalizes after each non-letter boundary, here after the hyphen.

howItWorks: PROPER treats any non-letter character (space, hyphen, punctuation) as a word boundary and uppercases the letter that follows it, while lowercasing all other letters.

howToSteps.name: Select the text
howToSteps.text: Click the cell with the text to fix.

limitations: Capitalizes after apostrophes, so "don't" becomes "Don'T" and "o'brien" becomes "O'Brien".
Does not respect proper nouns, acronyms, or brand casing (e.g. "iPhone" becomes "Iphone").
Operates only on a single text value.

commonErrors.cause: PROPER treats the apostrophe as a word boundary.
commonErrors.fix: Use a custom formula or post-edit for names like O'Brien and don't.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PROPER works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Why does PROPER break contractions?
faq.answer: It capitalizes the letter after every non-letter, including apostrophes, so "don't" becomes "Don'T".

faq.question: Does PROPER handle non-English text?
faq.answer: It follows Unicode letter boundaries but may not match language-specific title-case rules.

faq.question: How is PROPER different from UPPER?
faq.answer: UPPER uppercases everything; PROPER only uppercases the first letter of each word.
